key_insight: PanoLOG makes large outdoor 3D reconstruction feasible with panoramic images by replacing camera-frustum-based partitioning with geometry- and gradient-aware scene splitting. This avoids the collapse of block-wise optimization into expensive global training.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the high capture and computation cost of scaling 3D Gaussian Splatting to large outdoor scenes, especially when using panoramic ERP images whose 360° visibility breaks traditional local partitioning methods.
method: Uses panoramic equirectangular images to reduce data acquisition effort while preserving full-scene coverage.
Introduces a two-stage coarse-to-fine framework called PanoLOG for partitioning and optimizing large outdoor scenes.
Combines geometry cues and gradient-based signals to create effective blocks even when all cameras can see most of the scene.
Prevents block-wise optimization from degenerating into full global training by enforcing more meaningful local decomposition.
impact: For practitioners, this enables more scalable and efficient 3D reconstruction of large outdoor environments with fewer captures and lower training cost. It is especially relevant for robotics, AR/VR, mapping, and digital twin pipelines that need wide-area scene modeling.

paper_title: Geometry and Gradient-based Partitioning for Panoramic Outdoor Reconstruction
paper_authors: Weijian Chen, Weibo Yao, Yuhang Zhang, Xiaolin Tang, Guo Wang
